Yes. Your equality obstruction is sound, and the fixed-witness argument can be made quantitative. Taking the established ledgers in your question as inputs, I obtain
$$\boxed{\displaystyle d\le \left\lfloor\frac{8n}{121}\right\rfloor.}$$
Equivalently, for positive  $d$ ,
$$\boxed{\displaystyle n-13d\ge \frac{17}{8}\,d.}$$
Thus an explicit improved real denominator is
$$\frac{121}{8}=15.125>13.$$
The main new ingredient is the following exchange inequality:
$$\boxed{\displaystyle 3d\le c+s+b_2+b_3.}\tag{★}$$
I prove it below for an arbitrary permitted fixed witness assignment. It accounts for shared helpers and all permitted witness-to-witness edges. All vertices of  $U$  are omitted from the new dissociation constructions.1. Assessment of the proposed equality obstructionYour argument excluding  $n=13d$  for  $d>0$  is correct.Under the equality ledger, the  $2d$  labelled blocks are
$$a_j-x_j-c_j-y_j-b_j-i_j,$$
with  $a_j$  private,  $b_j$  helped, and each  $i_j$  having exactly one witness neighbour. Retaining all  $c_j,y_j,i_j$ , together with a dissociation set of the private-witness graph  $G[A]$ , gives
$$\beta_2(G)\ge 6d+\beta_2(G[A]).$$
Here  $G[A]$  is bipartite of maximum degree at most two. The component formulas
$$\beta_2(P_\ell)=\left\lceil\frac{2\ell}{3}\right\rceil,
\qquad
\beta_2(C_\ell)=\left\lfloor\frac{2\ell}{3}\right\rfloor$$
show that
$$\beta_2(G[A])\ge \frac{|A|}{2}=d,$$
with equality precisely when every component is a  $C_4$ . Since the equality ledger gives  $\beta_2(G)=7d$ , all private components must therefore be  $C_4$ 's.At that point every private witness has its owner edge and two edges inside  $A$ . Its degree capacity is exhausted, so there are no  $A$ -to- $B$  witness edges. This step handles the degree-two-witness issue correctly: full degree three is forced for the private witnesses only after the  $C_4$  conclusion. Helped witnesses may still have degree two.Your quotient orientation is also valid. Loops count twice toward degree and once toward indegree; an oriented loop chooses one of its two endpoint labels. Because the helped edges form a matching, distinct incoming quotient edges select distinct labels. Filling to two  $A$ -states per private  $C_4$  is consequently safe.There is a shorter way to finish that equality argument. Fix the original bipartition  $X,Y$ , and choose
$$\{a_j,c_j,y_j,i_j\}\quad\text{when }a_j\in X,$$
and
$$\{x_j,c_j,b_j,i_j\}\quad\text{when }a_j\in Y.$$
The retained private witnesses all lie in  $X$ , and the retained helped witnesses all lie in  $Y$ . Each family is independent, and saturation of the private witnesses excludes edges between the two families. Every block contributes four vertices, giving
$$\beta_2(G)\ge 8d>7d.$$
Thus the proposed integer strictness conclusion is valid. The quantitative proof below develops this two-colour idea further.2. A baseline and a set of private witnessesWrite  $\beta=\beta_2(G)$ . Continue to use the original fixed set  $W$ .Because  $\Delta(G)\le3$ , the selected nontrivial stars consist of: $c-s$  copies of  $P_3$ ; $s$  copies of  $K_{1,3}$ .Moreover, a  $q$ -centre cannot be a selected  $K_{1,3}$ -centre: its three selected leaves and its direct witness would give it at least four neighbours. $$N=c-q-s$$
clean selected  $P_3$ 's.For each clean selected  $P_3$ , label its vertices and fixed leaf witnesses as
$$a_j-x_j-c_j-y_j-b_j,$$
where  $a_j$  is one of the prescribed private witnesses. Thus its only neighbour in  $S$  is its owner  $x_j$ . The other witness  $b_j$  may be private or helped.Set
$$\mathcal A=\{a_j:1\le j\le N\},

$$\mathcal E=\{a\in\mathcal A:\deg_F(a)\le1\},
\qquad E=|\mathcal E|.$$
Directly from this definition,
$$\Delta(F[\mathcal E])\le1.$$
No path or cycle classification is needed for this observation.Now define a selected-vertex dissociation set  $D_0\subseteq S$ :On each clean  $P_3$ , retain  $c_j,y_j$ , omitting the private witness’s owner  $x_j$ .On each  $q$ - $P_3$ , retain its two leaves.On each selected  $K_{1,3}$ , retain its three leaves.Retain every selected isolate and every selected edge-component vertex.Its size is

$$D_0\cup\mathcal E$$

\end{aligned}\tag{3}$$

$$\deg_F(a)\le1.$$

Also, all its witness neighbours have the same bipartition colour. It can therefore require deletion in at most one of the two colour constructions.The total number of these deletions across both constructions is consequently at most
$$b_2+b_3.\tag{5}$$
This is where retaining shared helpers becomes inexpensive: a helper incident with three retained witnesses costs one vertex to remove.4.3 Full induced-edge checkAfter the two repairs, both resulting sets are dissociation sets:There are no edges between retained witnesses.Every retained witness’s active selected owner is omitted.Every retained witness has at most one isolate helper.Every retained isolate has at most one retained witness neighbour.In the selected-vertex portion, the clean  $P_3$  states retain a centre–leaf edge; the other star states retain independent vertices.Selected edge components remain matching edges.The fixed owner/helper rule excludes contacts from a retained witness to any other active selected vertex. $$2B_0+2c-s-E-b_2-b_3.$$

$$2d\le s+c-d+b_2+b_3.$$

$$\boxed{3d\le c+s+b_2+b_3.}\tag{★}$$

p=T'-g-2d,\qquad
v=2u+g-a,\qquad
H=b_3+\mu.$$

$$\boxed{

k={}&\frac52J+\frac52r+\frac72g+4p+2H\\
&+\frac{13}{4}s+\frac94q+m+z_0+\frac14D+\frac12v.
\end{aligned}}\tag{9}$$

$$d\le\Lambda,$$

\frac12(J+r+g+p)
+\frac32(b_3+\mu)
+\frac32s+\frac12q-\frac12D.

$$\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
8k-17\Lambda
={}&21J+2r+29g+33p+19b_3\\
&+10s+D+4v+8(m+z_0).
\end{aligned}}\tag{12}$$

$$17d\le17\Lambda\le8k=8(n-13d).$$

$$\boxed{121d\le8n}.$$

n\ge13d+\left\lceil\frac{17d}{8}\right\rceil.

$$n\ge13d+1,
\qquad
d\le\left\lfloor\frac{n-1}{13}\right\rfloor$$
follows. The latter also holds for nonpositive  $d$ , since a nonempty simple bipartite graph of minimum degree at least two has  $n\ge4$ .The new exchange also provides a short independent equality obstruction. Under the  $n=13d$  equality ledger,
$$c=2d,\qquad s=b_2=b_3=0.$$

$$3d\le2d,$$
